current_example.problem:
If the path $C$ is the line segment $\overline{AB}$ traversed from the point $A(0,0)$ to the point $B(1, 1),$ calculate the line integral 

$$
\displaystyle \int\limits_C x^2y\,\mathrm{d}x + xy\,\mathrm{d}y.
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $\mathbf{a} = 0\,\mathbf{i} + 0\,\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{b} = 1\,\mathbf{i} + 1\,\mathbf{j}.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =t\,i+t\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0 \le t \le 1.$ So, we have that $x(t) = t$ and $y(t) = t$ along the segment.

The derivative of $\mathbf r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}{x}^{2}y\,dx+xy\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}y\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+xy\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}y\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+xy\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{2}\cdot t\cdot 1+t\cdot t\cdot 1\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}\,dt \\  & ={[\frac{{t}^{4}}{4}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{7}{12}\end{aligned}
$$
